parsed.body:
The requested combination of properties cannot be satisfied. A comparison‑based sorting algorithm has a well‑known lower bound of Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case (see, e.g., the decision‑tree argument). Therefore it is impossible to achieve O(n) worst‑case time while still being comparison‑based. Moreover, any algorithm that attains O(n) worst‑case time must be non‑comparison‑based (such as counting sort or radix sort) and relies on assumptions about the key distribution, which violates the comparison‑based requirement. Consequently, no algorithm can simultaneously satisfy all four constraints: comparison‑based, O(n) worst‑case time, stable, and in‑place with O(1) extra space.

Given this impossibility, the appropriate response is to explain the theoretical limitation and suggest alternative approaches that relax one of the constraints, e.g., using radix sort for O(n) time (but non‑comparison‑based) or using mergesort for stability (O(n log n) time) while being in‑place with O(1) extra space via careful implementation.
